Q0121

William James

A verified English rendering from the curated archive.

Quotes / William James / Q0121

English

The essential achievement of the will is to attend to a difficult object and hold it fast before the mind.
Thinker William James
School Pragmatism
Source The Principles of Psychology (on will)
Theme Will
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with The Principles of Psychology (on will), within the tradition of Pragmatism. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of will, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In William James's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
